summary: Polygon's piece examines the state of VTubing, which grew on Twitch from 2019 and boomed after Hololive launched its English branch in 2020. Agencies like Hololive and Nijisanji offer financial security but impose restrictions, NDAs, and opaque graduations. An anonymous Nijisanji streamer and independent VTuber NagamiMugi both say the scene has become stale and needs more creative freedom for talents.
one_line: VTubing has grown saturated and stale, and interviewees say big agencies like Hololive and Nijisanji must give talents more creative freedom.
key_facts: VTubing gained popularity among English-speaking audiences on Twitch in 2019.
Cover Corporation launched the English branch of Hololive Production in 2020, bringing VTubing to wider North American and European markets.
Gawr Gura is the most subscribed-to Hololive talent to date.
Pokimane pivoted toward using a digital avatar weeks after Hololive's first English generation debuted.
Twitch reported VTubing-related content on the platform rose some 350% between January and August 2022.
Twitch's VTuber Takeover promotion most recently ran in August 2023.
In 2020, Hololive shuttered its Chinese division, graduating more than a handful of streamers.
Nijisanji announced the abrupt graduation of prominent talent Mysta Rias, who said he left due to burnout.
In August 2023, Cover Corporation announced two Holostars talents would graduate barely a year after debuting.
Nijisanji talents are under nondisclosure agreements that prevent them from explaining why they might be graduating, which is effectively retirement for VTubers.
Independent VTuber NagamiMugi says VTubing content has become 'kind of stale' and many VTubers are boxed into Minecraft or FPS games like Valorant.
One agency asked Mugi whether she would close her storefront business if she passed the interview phase.
Newer agencies such as Idol let talents create their own concepts, unlike Hololive and Nijisanji.
Hololive reported 50% growth in its 2023 financial report.
